docs.text: He was talking about the great lakes the other day - a wisconsinite
Ripped straight from the Trump playbook, Vivek Ramaswamy floated the idea of renaming one of the Great Lakes during a recent campaign appearance.

Yes, that's the closest thing I could think of...and it still makes no sense at all. Perhaps he was thinking of the Four Tops, who are in the Rock'n'Roll Hall of Fame, which is in Cleveland. Or that Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes, of where there are almost six.
Great Lakes people are built different lol I mean, there is a lot of Four Brothers that is fantastical delusion, but the way they knocked him out and dumped him under the ice was telling secrets.
He probably thought he was renaming one of the Great Lakes.
I think Strauss was also a Great Lakes Straussian to be fair, he ended up at UChicago
I heard he was changing the name of the Great Lakes to the Great Again Lakes.
Doubt he could even name the Great Lakes
Come on, you know he has no idea what the names are of any of the Great Lakes, let alone any of the Provinces or Territories.
Why did she tell him about the Great Lakes?? Now he’s gonna make the Great Lakes great again by renaming all of them.
Bill Maher did a joke suggesting what he'd rename the great lakes. Like "Lake Michigan, the State I won by A LOT" and "Lake White Superior" lol
We have it in a few places in Michigan, but Robert also has strong feelings about the Great Lakes too
No, I wouldn't expect that he repeat the wreck. It is just the most iconic Great Lakes name.
Bagger 288 makes new great lakes. Robert Evans destroys great lakes. And yet Robert Evans is a fan of Bagger 288...
Controversial opinion from Evans, not as controversial as blowing up the great lakes but still.
They are in the Mississippi River and indeed headed for the Great Lakes so he may well have talked to Gov Whitmer
You still have the Great Lakes, Robert. He can never take that from you.
He’d want you to note that it was a Great Lake, some say one of the five Great Lakes.
He singled that one out but started by mentioning the Great Lakes collectively

My bud has one of the 100 most-common male given names, shares his surname with over half a million other Americans. Of COURSE he has a namesake, who’s also a bass player, and also NOT HIM. Perhaps SLIGHTLY more accomplished, but at the same altitude, and on the West Coast, not the Great Lakes.
yes! Same with the Flatman—in the original, the words “deputy” and “Great Lakes” are in subscript because the JOKE is that he’s overinflating his importance
